answer.evidence: The drawing is a flat frontal elevation: horizontal beams at rows 4-6 and 17-19 are 1-3 row strips with no edge line and no eave shadow, so they read as vertical faces. The hanging sheaves at rows 7-16 and 20-27 are drawn face-on. Rows 0-3 hold only dark triangular pole tops over background. Nothing shows an ellipse, roof plane or visible contents seen from above, and the silhouette is a constant 48 px wide. There is no horizontal top surface and no receding side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of hanging rice bundles on a rack, drawn at small scale. Measured facts are 20 colours per tile (matching well-roofed, above hedge at 10), 0% flat-fill coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines carry a tint. Distinct colours total only 22, against 38-40 for the richer references (stall, well) and 11-14 for the simpler ones (hedge, bench, lamp). By eye, each bundle has a few yellow/ochre steps (about 4) plus a brown stem and a dark brown shadow, with some grain in the straw. The shading is repetitive: the same bundle is copied across the rack, and the rack frame is thin and barely shaded. It sits at or above the simple references (hedge, bench) but is below stall and well on ramp depth and per-object variety. It is acceptable next to the sparse and simple references, but I can't confirm it matches the richest ones, so it falls slightly short on density.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of hanging rice bundles on a rack, drawn small at the same scale as the references. The measured facts are solid: 20 colours per tile (the well has 20, the cheese stall 17, the hedge 10), 0% flat-fill coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline carries a tint (dark brown against the straw). It has only 22 distinct colours in total, compared with 38-40 for the well and stall, and by eye each bundle uses about 4 straw steps (pale yellow, gold, ochre, brown) with the rack posts in 2-3 brown tones. The bundles are repeated almost identically, with little per-bundle variation and little grain on the rack frame. It is not a sticker look and not flat, but it is shallower than the best references in ramp depth and variety, and the repeated shapes look somewhat mechanical. With the tinted outline and the tile density, a careful artist would likely accept it next to the hedge and the bench, though not quite at the level of the well or stall. Because of the doubt about the shallower ramps and the uniform repetition, this is borderline.
